notes: POST /v1/heartbeats protocol with ID rotation. Bootstrap: send an EMPTY heartbeat_id; the response returns a new ID. Each successful response returns a new ID to use for the following heartbeat. Cadence: every 5 seconds; if a valid heartbeat is not received within 10 seconds all open orders owned by those CLOB API credentials are canceled; the cancellation check runs every 5 seconds. On 400 Invalid Heartbeat ID the response supplies the expected ID and the client must send a fresh request using it. Heartbeat ids are synthetic placeholders. CONFLICT C-20 (docs/venue/verified-2026-10-05.md §11 and §H-3, VENUE-4; this note added by V2-9 on 2026-10-06, the examples unchanged): these examples follow the guide, which documents the 10-second cancellation for POST /v1/heartbeats (S-D20 lines 1485-1497; the CLOB OpenAPI sendHeartbeatV1, S-O02 line 4162). The CLOB OpenAPI keys the /v1/heartbeats 400 message error, not the guide's error_msg that the response-400-invalid-id-recovery example carries, and also documents a second route, POST /heartbeats (operationId sendHeartbeat: no body, 200 {status: ok}, no id), whose timing and relation to /v1/heartbeats are open (U-40). Neither the 400 key nor the route choice is settled by this fixture.
